projects.title:
DATA ENGINEERING -
Airflow ETL Pipeline
projects.tools: Apache Airflow, Python, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS instance

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.body:
Built a production ETL platform on Apache Airflow 2.8.1 (Docker Compose) that consolidates SQL Server and 10 third-party APIs into a single SQL Server warehouse, using a Bronze → Silver → Gold medallion architecture to move raw data through cleansing and business-ready transformation layers.

Platform runs 11 orchestrated DAGs on a weekly schedule, each following the same standardized extract → cleanse → transform pattern, feeding  gold-layer business tables used for downstream reporting.

blocks.heading: ROLE
blocks.body:
Designed the medallion architecture and DAG pattern (parallel bronze/silver extraction fanning into a single gold transform) that all 11 pipelines are built on.
Built the core SQL Server pipeline first — extracting 4 source tables and modeling them into 4 gold business tables (daily sales by SKU/channel, monthly channel performance, product catalog, unified daily product performance).

Wrote a shared Python data access layer (db_connection.py) handling chunked reads/writes, bulk-load performance tuning, automatic schema drift handling, and JSON serialization — reused across every pipeline instead of rebuilding logic per source.

Developed 10 API extractor modules (Amazon Ads, Amazon Vendor Central, Shopify, Zendesk, Klaviyo, Wayfair, BazaarVoice, Salsify, MySamm, Sage 300/HIP) on a shared base class handling auth, retries, and pagination. Implemented incremental/watermark-based loading (using python) so pipelines pull only new or changed records, with custom watermark logic where a source's default update behavior didn't fit.
Containerized the stack (custom Dockerfile with ODBC Driver 18) and wrote environment-driven connection bootstrap scripts for repeatable setup.
Documented the system end to end — an operator's manual for running/troubleshooting the stack and a full technical reference covering every DAG, script, and config variable

blocks.heading: Challenges & learnings
blocks.body:
SQL Server column/row limits on wide data: Salsify's product exports exceeded SQL Server's 1024-column and ~8060-byte row caps — solved by packing overflow fields into a JSON column instead of failing the load.

Data type incompatibility: pandas didn't support SQL Server's datetimeoffset type (ODBC type -155), breaking reads — resolved by casting to datetime2 at the query level.
Inconsistent incremental semantics across APIs: each platform tracked "updated" records differently (some by date, some by timestamp, some not reliably at all), requiring per-source watermark logic rather than one generic solution. 

API data bifurcation: The Sage 300/HIP integration had containerized/nested JSON information fields this required SQL command which required Column identification and separation into their own distinct columns. 

Schema drift from external APIs: incoming API fields changed shape or type over time (e.g., a column that was numeric started receiving text) — handled with automatic column widening and type migration in the write layer rather than manual fixes each time.

sections.heading: About
sections.body: Data Engineer specializing in ETL pipelines and Power BI reporting, with hands-on experience building production data platforms end-to-end. Designed a containerized Apache Airflow platform using a Bronze/Silver/Gold Medallion architecture to integrate 10+ REST/GraphQL APIs into a unified SQL Server warehouse, and delivered a ERP System-to-Power BI reporting pipeline with custom dimensional modelling and DAX measures — from source-system integration through to dashboard delivery and stakeholder-facing data quality troubleshooting.
